figures.caption: Fig. 1. Overview of TSCA-Net. A dual-stream input module fuses scene and trajectory features into a unified map I. The TSCA-Enhanced Goal Module produces an initial heatmap M(1), refined via Temporal-Spatial Clique Attention into M(2). The CPCP-AKGR Prediction Module decodes K=20 goal samples into full multimodal trajectories.

Fig. 3. Quantitative comparison against state-of-the-art methods. (a)-(b) Per-scene ADE/FDE on ETH/UCY (metres); dashed lines track TSCA-Net and MCK-Net trends. (c)-(d) ADE/FDE on SDD (pixels). Lower is better.
TABLE I QUANTITATIVE COMPARISON ON THE ETH/UCY BENCHMARK. RESULTS ARE REPORTED AS ADE/FDE (METRES). LOWER VALUES ARE BETTER. BOLD ENTRIES DENOTE THE BEST PERFORMANCE PER COLUMN.

Fig. 4. Qualitative results on ETH/UCY and SDD. Top: Predicted goal heatmaps overlaid on scene images (warmer = higher probability). Bottom: Predicted trajectory bundles (blue, K=20), best-of-20 (red), ground-truth (green), and observed history (grey). Best viewed in colour.
TABLE III COMPONENT-WISE ABLATION STUDY. RESULTS ARE REPORTED AS ADE/FDE (METRES) FOR ETH/UCY AND ADE/FDE (PIXELS) FOR SDD. LOWER VALUES ARE BETTER. BOLD ENTRIES DENOTE THE BEST PERFORMANCE.

TABLE IV ABLATION STUDY ON AKGR GRID RESOLUTION STRATEGY. RESULTS ARE REPORTED AS ADE/FDE (METRES) FOR ETH/UCY AND ADE/FDE (PIXELS) FOR SDD. LOWER VALUES ARE BETTER. BOLD ENTRIES DENOTE THE BEST PERFORMANCE.
